Part 3 · The Floor

Who Runs The Floor

About one move in five has no named mover ("a delegate moved") and is left out of the shares.

Types Of Floor Action

Every procedural move in the log, by kind. "Won" means the mover got what they asked for: a motion passed, a point of order was ruled well taken, an appeal overturned the chair. "Ruled out" means the chair ruled the move out of order. The minutes don't always record an outcome, so some moves are unclear.

Part 3 · Time On The Floor

Stunts, Jokes, Breaks & Shuffles

Hand-picked from the floor log. Jokes and stunts are moves made for a laugh or a point rather than business. Breaks and early stops are delegate motions to recess, take lunch, or quit for the day; working recesses (to count ballots or fix credentials or Zoom) and the chair's scheduled breaks are left out. Shuffles are motions to shorten or move lunch or reorder the agenda: well-meant or not, each one stops the business for a vote. The minutes record only some of this: no request about the air conditioning, a lost phone or a bathroom break appears in any of them.

Schedule & Agenda Shuffles

Motions to shorten or move lunch, change the day's hours, or take an item up ahead of its turn. Most need a two-thirds vote to suspend the rules, so even a well-meant one costs a second, often debate, and a vote.

The Rosters

One roster per convention. Each person is counted once a year: as a delegate if they were listed as both delegate and alternate.

YearListedDelegatesAlternatesAttendedAttendance Record

Method. Rosters are the national party's delegate spreadsheets for 2006–2022 (2014 split into credentialed and no-show sheets), the roster in the 2024 minutes' Appendix D, and the 2026 Final Credentials Report (Appendix C, people marked Removed left out). There is no roster for 2008. People are matched across years by first and last name, with common nicknames treated as one name (Bill and William), and not by state, since people move and some serve on another state's delegation. A name change, such as after marriage, is missed, which understates retention; two people with the same common name are counted as one, which overstates it. 2020 is the May online session's list. For the state view, a person counts with the delegation they came with each year; where the 2026 report lists someone on several delegations, the first is used. The five attendance groups list a person under every state they came with.
